# BAD-078 — A pure-move harness should account for every line, not a table of named blocks

## Brief
BAD-047's movecheck.mjs is the best instrument the repo has for proving a move changed nothing, and more moves are coming — BAD-052, BAD-053 and BAD-054 all landed the same week. But its design has two blind spots that the next split will inherit: it verifies a table of 37 named keys, so anything the table does not name is invisible; and it drops the two gates' trailing 'return { … };' before diffing, which is precisely where the spike's risk 6 lives (loadRoom must hand back the object it mutated, never a copy). A future harness should account for every line of the old file — the complement of what it matched must be empty and named — rather than confirming a list. That is what BADS-047/Snowden did by hand with an orphan-line sweep, and it is the check that would have needed no hand.

Evidence: Proved by perturbation on a scratch copy, not argued. With the entire 42-line header doc deleted from index.ts AND loadRoom changed to 'collab: { ...collab }' — the exact bug risk 6 names — movecheck printed 'RESULT: clean (37 moved, 0 inline)' and exited 0. Three section-4 rows have no key at all: the header doc (old 22-63), the retired-blanket-gate comment (790-792) and 'return fail(unknown_mode, 400)' (1229). All three are correct in this PR; I diffed them by hand and they are byte-identical. The harness bites hard on what it does cover — a status code changed inside pull.ts printed 'DIFF download-url' with the unified diff, and a deleted dispatch line printed NO-DISPATCH, both exit 1.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus builds the harness, then one reviewer on opus audits it. Both fable-tier personas run on opus: Fable's weekly limit is reached (Eric, 2026-09-15).

Eric's two calls, 2026-09-15, before any member was planned:

- **A committed tool with npm test coverage**, not a throwaway. `scripts/movecheck.mjs` plus `test/movecheck.test.js`, so the instrument's own bite is proved by test cases that run on every `npm test` rather than by a hand perturbation run each time it is used. That is the whole lesson of BAD-047: the harness was written by the people it judged, it broke once mid-PR, and its blind spots were found only because a reviewer perturbed a scratch copy by hand.
- **Land BAD-078 on its own, now**; the four queued Electron splits it would have protected (BAD-041 renderer/app.js, BAD-042 main.js, BAD-043 renderer/creator.js, BAD-048 the release-note art) stay queued and are not a prerequisite either way: Eric expects to move away from releasing an Electron app as the web and iOS apps get streamlined, so those splits may never run. The harness is therefore justified by the splits that ALREADY LANDED, which are also its test corpus, and by the web/ and server/ moves most likely to come next — not by a future Electron split.

Priority stays P2. Eric de-prioritized the splits rather than elevating this.

## Outcome
Landed 2026-09-16 as https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/381, squash-merged to main as 5472ff0. `scripts/movecheck.mjs` over seven modules in `scripts/movecheck/`, `test/movecheck.test.js` (40 tests), six waiver fixtures and a corpus definition in `test/fixtures/movecheck/`, one npm script, one CLAUDE.md line, and `fetch-depth: 0` on the three CI jobs that run `npm test`.

The tool answers, for every line of a pre-split file, where that line went. Clean only when the old-side complement is empty and the new side is fully traced, with each remainder in a category printed by name. Parser-free: a longest-first matcher finds contiguous runs of old lines in one new file at a constant indent delta and consumes each new line, so nothing accounts for two old lines and the unclaimed remainder is the split's additions for free. Comments are deliberately not forgiven, since a deleted header doc is one of the two bugs it exists to catch; reworded prose goes through a waiver that pins text, carries a printed reason, and fails when it matches nothing.

Three audit rounds, and the first two found the SAME defect shape — a category that reads a line's prefix and never asks what follows, which exempts the rest of the line on both sides and yields a report byte-identical to a verified baseline at exit 0. Russet found it in the header rule; Lamoka found it still live in the two largest forgiving categories, because round one's fix was scoped to the attack rather than the rule; Osprey found a third instance introduced by round two's own fix. The structural answer is that tests now pin rules by mutation — nine narrower patches are each caught. Both of BAD-047's original perturbations, which the predecessor passed at exit 0, now exit 1 and name their lines; ten attacks bite where all ten passed before.

CI then found the assumption nobody had tested: the harness refused to borrow `admin/node_modules/typescript` on the argument that a committed tool must not die on a fresh clone, and then depended on git history, which a shallow `actions/checkout` does not have. All three `npm test` jobs now fetch it, `release.yml`'s included — that one had never failed and fires on a tag, not a pull request.

Verified on main after the merge: BAD-047 reads clean at 1230/1230, exit 0. In CI, all six corpus splits ran and passed rather than skipping.

Filed on the way: BAD-088 (P3), the `collab/room.ts:19-21` comment giving a false mechanism for a real property; SPD-095 (P3), the Bash hook refusing a clone into scratch, which is the friction that made a brief of Spud's promise a member something Law 7 forbids.

Seven spudagents, $121 at API list price.
